claims.text: Partial substitution with Mo will improve the elevated-temperature mechanical performance of the titanium- and nickel-containing high-entropy alloy relative to the Mo-free baseline.
The target initial material is a single-phase solid-solution high-entropy alloy in which Ti and Ni are primary constituents.
The target material is similar in alloy system to AlCo1−xFeNiTi.
Approximately 5–10 at.% Mo will be substituted for a primary element such as Fe.
The proposed operating boundary is approximately 500–900°C.
Mo atoms have a larger atomic size and different bonding characteristics in the proposed alloy context.
Mo substitution is expected to increase lattice distortion.
Mo substitution may promote formation of Mo-rich nanoclusters.
Mo-induced lattice distortion and Mo-rich nanoclusters can obstruct dislocation motion.
Mo incorporation is hypothesized to produce solid-solution strengthening.
Mo incorporation may alter local chemical ordering.
The proposed lattice distortion, local ordering, and possible nanoclusters are expected to improve high-temperature yield strength.
The proposed lattice distortion, local ordering, and possible nanoclusters are expected to improve creep resistance.
The Mo-substituted alloy is expected to have higher yield strength than the Mo-free baseline at elevated temperature.
The Mo-substituted alloy is expected to have a lower creep rate than the Mo-free baseline at elevated temperature.
The anticipated yield-strength improvement is approximately 10–20%.
The Mo-free baseline has comparatively lower elevated-temperature mechanical performance.
The hypothesis applies to compositions similar to AlCo1−xFeNiTi.
